title: Good decision: Lagged broadcast messages silently skipped, not errored
description:
Decision: When a BroadcastStream receiver falls behind and messages are dropped, the Lagged error is logged and skipped (returns None), not propagated to close the stream.

Code location: lines 174-180 of kithd/src/events.rs. Test: test_lagged_receiver_skips in kith-events/src/lib.rs.

Why this is correct: A lagged receiver indicates a slow client, not a service error. Terminating the stream (propagating the error) forces the client to reconnect, re-authenticate, and re-establish the subscription. This creates a cascade of reconnections and may cause more event loss under load. Skipping gracefully allows the client to keep the stream open and resync via /changes at its own pace, with fewer round-trips.

The client learns it was lagged when it calls /changes and gets a state delta, not through stream closure. This is more resilient.

The wrong alternative would be to propagate Lagged as a stream error (Err(e)) or return a 500 and close the connection. This increases load and breaks the stream unnecessarily.
